import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a custom order for customer_age_group for better visualization
# This ensures age groups are plotted in a logical sequence (e.g., youngest to oldest)
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Calculate total sales by customer age group
sales_by_age = df.groupby('customer_age_group')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='customer_age_group', y='total', data=sales_by_age, palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Customer Age Group', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels if they overlap, and align them to the right
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add data labels on top of the bars for exact values
for index, row in sales_by_age.iterrows():
    plt.text(index, row['total'], f'{row["total"]:.2f}', color='black', ha="center", va='bottom')

# Improve layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
